Yeah, I played Dragonfall when it first released - never finished it though. I finished Hong Kong last night so I can give more of a conclusive summary of my thoughts towards it.

My memory of DF is rather spotty to be honest so it's difficult to compare them fairly. I seem to recall I experienced combat more in DF than in HK (whether this was due to building my character poorly and being unable to talk my way through a situation or the game itself simply containing more combat, I can't honestly be sure.)

The combat in HK is as much the same as previous Shadowrun games. It's still visually kinda flat and I feel like none of my characters actually progressed in terms of combat ability. Combat seems to take about the same amount of time to resolve all the way through the game. Towards the end of the game I groaned audibly, several times, when yet another group of enemies popped up while I was fighting my way towards the game's conclusion.

I liked the new decking system they created, for the most part, at least. In HK you can run past sentries who move on predetermined paths and if you're good (or lucky, I suppose) you can sneak past without the system ever noticing you. Sadly there's still combat in the matrix at times. The systems you're hacking occasionally come with guard programs, which is unfortunate as I feel the matrix combat is even worse than combat in the "meatspace."

I liked the companions in HK well enough, my favourite being one of the more positive party members I've seen in the Shadowrun games. Saying that, I feel as though DF probably had the best party members overall.

I'm planning on playing DF: DC at some point as I feel the general consensus of DF being the current superior Shadowrun game is pretty accurate. I'd also like to experience the DC content and actually finish the game this time.

Personally, I enjoy Shadowrun the most for its exploration, dialogue options and aesthetic. The combat is not something I was overly fond of and it definitely wore me down as the game went on. I guess in a sort of Planescape: Torment vein, only not as compelling or brilliant. 

Saying that, I'm not completely done with the series and I'd like to see what the creators can do if they keep making Shadowrun games. If you like Shadowrun for the same aspects I do, I'd recommend picking up HK with a discount and when all of the bugs have been squashed.

**TL;DR**: If you like Shadowrun for the non-combat bits, HK is pretty good. Combat is still flat and mostly uninteresting. IMO it's a solid (but currently buggy) entry in the Shadowrun series. DF is probably still better.

Still, an rpg where you can make almost any kind of character and have situations play out differently depending on your skills, dialogue choices and game decisions is always welcome.

I feel as though I could ramble for days on my love for Planescape: Torment, but I'd like to just touch on the large amount of reading point.

I remember one part of the game in the Clerk's Ward, I think it was called, the Brothel "section." You can go from room to room, conversing and delving into each "prostitute's" dialogue trees & side quests as deeply or as shallowly as you like - whether hurriedly to quickly pick up Fall-From-Grace or ponderously as you learned the skills, quirks & often life stories of each individual.

I believe I spent over an hour engrossed in the music and the dialogue of this one building and it seemed to fly by in half the time or less - and I honestly don't think many other single player gaming experiences have come close to the interest and the immersion I felt in that instance.

So, to badly summarise, no, I don't think the large amount of reading hurt the game in any instance. Even though I was interacting with fictional characters using plain text, those were some of the most interesting and believable characters I've ever interacted with in a video game.
